Trial showed motor skill improvement vs. decline in placebo group (statistically significant)

title: Physicists directly observe quantum gravity effects on ultracold atoms
summary: Researchers directly observed a quantum effect of gravity predicted by Einstein using ultracold atoms split between a held position and free fall.

title: Scientists discover human heart muscle can regenerate after heart attack
summary: Researchers at Australian institutions demonstrated for the first time that human heart muscle cells can regenerate after a heart attack, challenging decades of assumption that cardiac tissue loss is permanent. While a single heart attack can destroy up to one-third of heart cells and scarring limit
takeaways: First demonstration of cardiac regeneration in human heart tissue, not just mice
Single heart attack can destroy up to one-third of heart cells
Findings published in Circulation Research
Natural regenerative response exists but insufficient to replace all damaged muscle

title: Semaglutide shown to slow aging and extend lifespan in mice
summary: Semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, extended lifespan by nearly 100 days in older mice while improving memory, muscle function, and reducing aging markers, according to an NIH-funded UC Berkeley study. The drug outperformed calorie restriction in memory and blood-sugar control,
takeaways: Median lifespan extended by nearly 100 days in treated mice
Improved memory, muscle function, blood sugar control, and reduced inflammation
Outperformed calorie restriction in exploratory behavior and spatial memory
Metabolic rate remained unchanged (unlike calorie restriction)
Suggests separate aging pathway beyond appetite suppression

title: AstraZeneca breast cancer pill fails in pivotal trial
summary: AstraZeneca's camizestrant (Etcamah) failed its pivotal SERENA-4 trial, showing no improvement in progression-free survival compared to standard treatment for advanced ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. The drug had received accelerated FDA approval in early September 2026 for resistant tumor
takeaways: Camizestrant failed SERENA-4 pivotal trial on September 12, 2026
No improvement in progression-free survival vs. standard treatment
Drug received accelerated FDA approval weeks earlier (early September 2026)
Company continuing early-stage disease testing despite first-line market setback

title: Scientists Identify Method to Breach Pancreatic Cancer's Immune Shield
summary: Researchers at University of Miami's Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center found that blocking IL1RAP, an inflammatory receptor, can disrupt pancreatic tumors' protective immune shield and enhance treatment effectiveness. The team is planning a first-of-its-kind neoadjuvant clinical trial combining
takeaways: IL1RAP inhibition reduced tumor-protecting immune-suppressive cells and decreased fibrosis
Increased T cell activity in preclinical experiments
IL1RAP functions as shared control point linking tumor cells, immune cells, and fibroblasts
First-of-its-kind neoadjuvant clinical trial planned with chemoimmunotherapy
Targets pancreatic tumors' paradox: highly inflamed yet immune-suppressive

title: UCLA develops cancer-fighting T cells from cord blood for solid tumors
summary: UCLA researchers engineered T cells from cord blood stem cells that attacked solid tumors in mice while avoiding graft-versus-host disease. These AlloESO-T cells use TCR therapy to recognize cancer proteins and can be manufactured in frozen batches, addressing cost and production-time barriers that
takeaways: AlloESO-T cells successfully controlled ovarian cancer and melanoma in mice with single dose
TCR therapy detects internal protein fragments, broader than CAR T-cell approach
Current personalized T-cell therapy costs six figures and takes weeks to produce
Cord blood cells enable pre-manufactured frozen batches for multiple patients
Published in Cell Reports Medicine

title: Roivant lung disease drug achieves mid-stage trial success
summary: Roivant's experimental drug mosliciguat met primary endpoints in a Phase 2 trial for pulmonary hypertension, showing a 56% reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance versus placebo. The results exceeded expectations and position the drug as a potential new therapeutic approach and possible second bl
takeaways: 56% placebo-adjusted reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance
35-meter placebo-adjusted improvement in six-minute walk distance
53% placebo-adjusted reduction in NT-proBNP, a heart failure marker
16-week Phase 2 trial achieved primary and secondary endpoints

title: Researchers discover potent antivenom from rattlesnake blood proteins
summary: Scientists found that combinations of toxin-blocking proteins naturally present in rattlesnake blood are about 10 times more effective than current commercial antivenoms.

title: Semaglutide linked to 21% lower psychiatric hospitalization risk in bipolar disorder
summary: A large Swedish study of nearly 15,000 people with bipolar disorder found that semaglutide use (Ozempic, Wegovy) was associated with a 21% lower risk of psychiatric hospitalization.

title: Scientists discover immune 'off switch' that stops inflammation
summary: Researchers at University College London identified epoxy-oxylipins, natural immune molecules that brake inflammation by preventing excessive accumulation of intermediate monocytes. A clinical trial of drug GSK2256294 showed it increased these molecules, accelerated pain resolution, and reduced infl
takeaways: Epoxy-oxylipins are fat-derived molecules that naturally suppress excessive immune activation
Trial enrolled 48 healthy volunteers receiving placebo or sEH-blocking drug GSK2256294
Drug increased epoxy-oxylipin levels and sharply reduced intermediate monocytes in blood and tissue
Findings suggest therapeutic targets for arthritis, heart disease, and diabetes

title: FDA-approved AI tool detects severe heart attacks and rare coronary blockage patterns on EKGs
summary: The FDA granted rare de novo classification to Powerful Medical's 'Queen of Hearts' algorithm, an AI tool for detecting severe heart attacks and unusual coronary blockage patterns on EKGs. De novo classification, granted fewer than 10 times per year, indicates a novel device requiring substantial cl
takeaways: FDA issued de novo classification (granted fewer than 10 times per year)
Detects both acute myocardial infarction and unusual coronary obstruction indicators on EKGs
Intended for triage of chest pain patients to appropriate cardiac care

title: Nighttime Light Exposure Linked to Heart Changes and Reduced Function
summary: A study of over 11,000 UK Biobank participants found that nighttime light exposure above 3 lux correlated with cardiac remodeling—thickened left ventricular walls and reduced heart flexibility—three years after measurement. Researchers characterized these as early signs of diminished heart function
takeaways: Study of 11,071 participants tracked via wrist-worn light sensors over seven days
Nighttime light exposure above 3 lux linked to cardiac remodeling and thickening
Changes detected in left and right ventricles and left atria
MRI scans conducted three years after light exposure measurement
Published September 9, 2026, in European Heart Journal

title: Study of 117-Year-Old Reveals Simultaneous Extreme Aging and Youth
summary: A comprehensive multi-omic study of Maria Branyas, who lived to 117, revealed she simultaneously exhibited extreme aging markers and powerful biological protection mechanisms. The research suggests extreme longevity involves pronounced aging signs alongside traits protecting against aging's harmful
takeaways: Most comprehensive biological investigation yet of a supercentenarian
Multi-omic analysis used genomic, proteomic, epigenomic, metabolomic, microbiomic data
Branyas had very short telomeres and pro-inflammatory immune system, yet low actual inflammation
Epigenetic biological age younger than chronological age of 117
Gut microbiome dominated by beneficial bifidobacteria
Published in Cell Reports Medicine

title: U.S. cancer medicine shortages persist, forcing treatment workarounds
summary: An ongoing shortage of cancer medications continues disrupting treatment at leading U.S. cancer centers and clinical trials, according to a National Comprehensive Cancer Network survey of 34 treatment centers. All centers reported experiencing at least one medication shortage; 61% manage through inv
takeaways: All 34 surveyed NCCN centers reported shortages of at least one medicine
Over 20% reported shortages of five or more medications
61% able to treat despite shortages (by avoiding waste and reducing dosing)
Two-thirds report treatment delays due to insurance prior authorization requirements

title: UniQure to Release Four-Year Results for Huntington's Gene Therapy
summary: UniQure is expected to announce four-year clinical trial results for AMT-130, its Huntington's disease gene therapy, before the end of September 2026. Earlier three-year results showed the high dose slowed Huntington's progression by 75% compared to matched external controls; the drug has already be
takeaways: Four-year results expected by end of September 2026
Three-year data showed 75% slowing of Huntington's progression (high-dose cohort of 12 patients vs. external controls)
Already submitted for regulatory approval in U.S. and U.K.

title: Platinum chemotherapy in childhood causes cellular aging in liver tissue
summary: A study published in Science found that platinum-based chemotherapy given to children with hepatoblastoma accelerated cellular aging in liver tissue, potentially increasing long-term risk of secondary tumors. While platinum agents improved five-year survival from 20% to over 80%, lifelong monitoring
takeaways: Average 2,200 mutations per liver sample; typical of adult livers
Mutation load increased proportionally with cisplatin/carboplatin exposure
Mutations affect cancer-related genes and pathways associated with other pathologies
Childhood liver cells aged to adult-equivalent level
Five-year survival improved from 20% to 80% for localized tumors
Lifelong monitoring of survivors recommended for late-onset malignancies

title: ARPA-H invests $62 million in FDA-authorized AI for heart failure treatment
summary: ARPA-H committed $62.7 million to develop FDA-authorized AI systems for heart failure treatment through the ADVOCATE program. The initiative targets 6.7 million Americans with heart failure, particularly in underserved rural areas, with AI agents to assess symptoms, prescribe drugs, and order tests.
takeaways: $62.7 million total investment
$33.7 million in first-year awards to Atman Health, UpDoc, Tempus AI, Stanford, Duke, Kaiser Permanente
Up to $29 million additional funding available
Targets 6.7 million Americans with heart failure

title: Early statin use linked to 15% lower dementia risk in type 2 diabetes patients
summary: A Danish study of over 132,000 people found that starting statins within a year of type 2 diabetes diagnosis reduced dementia risk by 15% over 10 years.

title: AstraZeneca's experimental COPD drug shows strong late-stage trial results
summary: AstraZeneca's experimental COPD treatment demonstrated competitive efficacy in late-stage clinical studies with potential market differentiation.

title: Inhibrx achieves first success for long-elusive immunotherapy target
summary: Inhibrx reported the first positive result for a previously difficult immunotherapy target despite repeated failures in the field.

title: Researchers Identify New Weakness in Treatment-Resistant Prostate Cancer
summary: Scientists discovered a strategy to attack treatment-resistant prostate cancers by targeting cells that evade therapy through identity changes.

title: Immune Signal Discovered That Promotes Spinal Cord Regeneration
summary: Researchers have identified a neutrophil-derived immune signal (IL-4) that suppresses inflammation and enables spinal cord nerve fibers to regrow in zebrafish models.

title: Oxalate compound in healthy foods may worsen inflammatory bowel disease
summary: Researchers found that oxalates in foods like spinach and almonds may aggravate gut inflammation in people with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

title: Long-lived bats' genetic strategies may reveal human longevity secrets
summary: Researchers studying long-lived bat species have identified genetic mechanisms combining powerful immune defenses with cell-damage elimination that could inform strategies to extend human healthspan.

title: Time-restricted eating shows promise for Type 1 diabetes control
summary: A small study found that eating only during an 8-hour window (noon to 8 p.m.) improved blood sugar control in adults with Type 1 diabetes and obesity.

title: Novartis and Novo Nordisk cardiovascular drug failures signal emerging headwinds across the sector
summary: Back-to-back clinical failures from major pharmaceutical companies may dampen industry confidence and reduce investment in cardiovascular drug development.

title: Long-term health impacts of 9/11 persist for thousands of patients, says NYC thoracic surgeon
summary: A thoracic surgeon in New York City describes how the Sept. 11 attack continues to affect thousands of patients' health decades later.

title: Cancer Drug Shortages Continue to Disrupt Patient Care
summary: Platinum chemotherapy drug shortages are interrupting cancer patient treatment across healthcare systems.

title: Ontario Study: Medication Side Effects Trigger Unnecessary New Prescriptions
summary: A major study from Ontario identified 24 common medication chains where one drug's side effects can prompt prescriptions for unrelated conditions, potentially creating harmful cascades.

title: Opinion: Autonomous AI Will Outperform Physician-Assisted Care by 2030
summary: Ezekiel J. Emanuel and Abe Baker-Butler argue that autonomous AI systems will surpass both unaided physicians and human-AI collaborative teams on core medical tasks within five years.

summary: Despite FDA approval of the new pancreatic cancer drug Rasonque, some patients face barriers in obtaining access to the breakthrough treatment.

summary: Novo Nordisk discontinued two clinical trials of a drug designed to reduce inflammation and improve cardiovascular health outcomes.

title: Trump Administration Proposes AI Solutions to Address Rural Healthcare Workforce Shortages

title: President dangles $500 ACA refunds for select enrollees before midterms

title: AMA CEO: AI Will Augment Rather Than Replace Physicians
